q: The Daniell integral extends the Lebesgue integral by starting from a lattice of functions and a positive linear functional. Its advantage over the Lebesgue approach is:
opts: It allows construction of integrals on spaces without a pre-existing σ-algebra — the σ-algebra is derived from the integral
It gives a different result than Lebesgue for L¹ functions
exp: Daniell's approach: start with (X, L, I) where L is a vector lattice of functions and I is a positive linear functional. Extend by monotone convergence. The measure is recovered a posteriori: μ(A) = I(1_A). This is basis for integration on locally compact spaces (Riesz representation) without first specifying a σ-algebra.
